The simple
method.

Weight management is influenced by many factors. Start with the basics: nourishing food, regular movement, adequate sleep and consistency.

01 / EAT

Build better meals

Include protein, vegetables, fruit, whole grains and foods you genuinely enjoy. Balanced meals can make healthy eating easier to sustain.

02 / MOVE

Move more often

Walk, lift, bike, swim or play. Choose activities that fit your life and gradually increase what you can comfortably do.

03 / REPEAT

Stay consistent

One off day doesn't erase your progress. Return to your routine at the next meal, walk or workout.

Eat without
overthinking it.

A good eating routine doesn't have to be perfect. The goal is to make nutritious choices easier while leaving room for foods you enjoy.

Build a balanced plate

At many meals, try combining several food groups instead of relying on one “perfect” food.

  • A source of protein
  • Vegetables or fruit
  • A satisfying carbohydrate
  • A little healthy fat

Make it convenient

Keep simple options available for busy days so convenience doesn't automatically mean skipping a meal.

  • Greek yogurt or cottage cheese
  • Eggs, beans or pre-cooked chicken
  • Frozen vegetables and fruit
  • Whole-grain wraps or rice
Remember: You don't need to eliminate entire food groups or label individual foods as “good” or “bad” to make progress.

Move in a
way you like.

Regular activity can support health, fitness and weight management. Start at a level you can recover from and build gradually.

ActivityEasy starting pointHow to progress
Walking10–20 minutesAdd a few minutes or another day
Strength training2 short sessions/weekAdd repetitions or resistance gradually
Cycling15–20 minutesIncrease duration at a comfortable pace
Sports / recreationOne activity you enjoyPlay more regularly

Your first
7 days.

Use this as a flexible starting point. You can repeat it, modify it, or ignore anything that doesn't fit your life.

DAY 01

Set the baseline

Think about your current eating, movement and sleep habits without judging yourself.

DAY 02

Upgrade one meal

Choose one meal and make it more balanced and filling.

DAY 03

Take a walk

Add an easy walk or another activity you enjoy.

DAY 04

Plan tomorrow

Decide what you'll eat and when you'll move before the day gets busy.

DAY 05

Protect your sleep

Create a calmer evening routine and aim for a consistent bedtime.

DAY 06

Keep going

Don't compensate for an off-plan meal by starving or punishing yourself with exercise.

Day 07: Review the week. Keep the habits that felt realistic and change the ones that didn't.
Practical tips

Small moves that make a big difference.

You do not need a perfect week. Focus on repeatable habits that make the next healthy choice easier.

01

Build meals around protein + plants

Try a protein source, vegetables or fruit, and a satisfying high-fiber carb. This can make meals more filling without turning food into a math problem.

02

Make drinks work for you

Choose water, sparkling water, unsweetened tea, or other low-calorie drinks most of the time. Liquid calories can add up quickly.

03

Start walking where you are

Even short walks count. Begin with a comfortable amount and gradually add time or distance as your body adapts.

04

Use the 80% rule

A missed workout or restaurant meal does not erase progress. Get back to your normal routine at the next opportunity.

05

Make the easy choice visible

Keep fruit, water, yogurt, vegetables, or other go-to foods easy to grab. Put less-helpful impulse foods farther away or buy smaller amounts.

06

Track trends, not single days

Body weight naturally moves up and down. Look at longer-term trends and pair them with energy, activity, sleep, and how consistently you followed your plan.

Important: If you have significant medical conditions, take medications affected by weight or diet, or have a history of an eating disorder, talk with a qualified healthcare professional before making major changes.

FAQ

Quick answers to common questions about getting started.

Do I need a strict diet?

No. A sustainable approach generally works better when it fits your preferences and routine.

How quickly should I expect results?

It varies by person. Weight can change from week to week, so focus on longer-term trends and habits.

Do I have to exercise?

Physical activity has important health benefits and can support weight management, but your routine can start small.

What if I have a medical condition?

Talk with a qualified healthcare professional before making major changes to your diet or activity, especially if you have a medical condition or take medication.
